It does not assert informal part (b), `e_n s_μ = ... vertical n-strip`, so this declaration alone cannot imply the full informal statement. The separately declared `SymmetricFunctions.pieri_vertical` is attached to the same market statement, but it is not part of `pieri_horizontal`'s meaning. Q2: Yes, the informal conjunction of (a) and (b) implies part (a). The formal definitions otherwise match that part: `NPartition` has `parts : Fin N → ℕ` with weak decrease; `horizontalNStripPartitions` filters for containment, `isHorizontalStripFun`, and size equation `|λ| = |μ| + n`; `hsymm` is documented as the sum of all degree-n monomials; and `schur` is defined as `∑ T ∈ ssytFinset lam, T.toMonomial`. Thus the difference enters in the result proposition of `SymmetricFunctions.pieri_horizontal`, not in a binder or referenced definition. To make it faithful to the entire informal statement, use one declaration whose conclusion conjoins both the horizontal and vertical equations, or split the informal statement into separate (a) and (b) statement IDs and associate `pieri_horizontal` only with (a) and `pieri_vertical` only with (b).

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.det.det.justification: Q1: yes. Q2: yes. The elaborated signature quantifies over `{R : Type u} [CommRing R]`, `{n : ℕ}`, and `A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R`, matching the determinant chapter's ambient commutative ring K and arbitrary n×n matrices. The informal restricted inner sum, “`Q ⊆ [n]; |P|=|Q|`,” is represented exactly by the formal sum over every Q followed by `if h : Q.card = P.card then ... else 0`. The definitions also have the intended meanings: `finsetSumFin P := ∑ i ∈ P, i.val`, and `submatrixDet A P Q h := (A.submatrix (P.orderEmbOfFin rfl) (Q.orderEmbOfFin (h ▸ rfl))).det`, so its first subset selects rows and its second selects columns. Although the formal summand is written `submatrixDet A Q P h * submatrixDet B Qᶜ Pᶜ ...`, while the informal summand is `det(sub_P^Q A) · det(sub_P̃^Q̃ B)`, the two complete double sums coincide by globally exchanging the dummy variables P and Q; the cardinality condition and exponent `finsetSumFin P + finsetSumFin Q` are symmetric under that exchange. The use of `Fin n` gives zero-based representatives rather than the informal one-based `[n]`, but shifting every selected index by one changes the exponent by `P.card + Q.card = 2 * P.card` on the cardinality-restricted terms, so the factor `(-1)^(sum P + sum Q)` is unchanged. Complements and increasing-order submatrices likewise correspond under this identification. Thus the Lean equality and the informal equality are equivalent in both directions.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.pier.justification: The target faithfully formalizes only clause (a): `MvPolynomial.hsymm (Fin N) R n * SymmetricFunctions.schur mu = ∑ lam ∈ SymmetricFunctions.horizontalNStripPartitions mu n, SymmetricFunctions.schur lam`, where the indexing definition enforces containment, the horizontal-strip inequalities, and size difference `n`. However, the informal statement also asserts clause (b), namely `e_n s_μ` as a sum over vertical `n`-strips. No vertical-strip/elementsymmetric equality occurs in the target conclusion. Thus the full informal statement implies the target's horizontal clause, but the target does not express the full two-part informal statement. The difference enters in the conclusion of `SymmetricFunctions.pieri_horizontal`; to make the package faithful, either associate this declaration only with informal clause (a), or replace/augment the formal statement with a conjunction including the vertical Pieri equality (using definitions of `e_n` and vertical-strip partitions).

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.det.det.justification: The formal outer sums `∑ P, ∑ Q, if h : Q.card = P.card then ... else 0` are equivalent to summing over `P ⊆ [n]` and only those `Q` with `|P| = |Q|`; the additional terms are zero. Also, `finsetSumFin` is exactly the required `sum P`/`sum Q`, and finset complement is complement inside `Fin n`. Although the target calls `submatrixDet A Q P`, whose body restricts rows to `Q` and columns to `P`, while the informal RHS writes `sub_P^Q A` (rows `P`, columns `Q` under the supplied definition), this does not change the complete double sum: exchanging the dummy variables `P` and `Q` converts the formal RHS into the informal RHS. The sign and cardinality condition are symmetric, and `Qᶜ, Pᶜ` simultaneously become `Pᶜ, Qᶜ`. Thus each displayed equality implies the other. The formal `CommRing R` is the standard scalar structure needed here and imposes no unrelated mathematical hypothesis.
